evidence.note: Set explicit >=45% target and a standing rule to eval each checkpoint and write the best to /app/best_checkpoint.txt — establishes the tracking/persistence discipline up front.
Repeated 'save best / update best checkpoint pointer' immediately after evals across every stage — best checkpoint persisted the moment a new best appears.
'Kill old run' and 'Confirm best, kill round 4' — detects non-improving/dead runs and stops spending budget on them.
Re-verifies top candidates and commits/finalizes m8-200 — keeps a validated best-known checkpoint safely persisted as fallback.
Time/timer is checked only a handful of times over ~380 steps — clock awareness exists but is sparse, not continuous budget reconciliation.

reasoning: The agent maintains an implicit ledger of named runs (mix, m4–m8) evaluated stepwise, updates /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately on each new best, and detects stalled runs by killing dead rounds — matching anchor 8. It does not reach 10 because clock checks are infrequent and there is no observable quantification of marginal gain per run or explicit reasoning about whether the target is reachable in the remaining time. Time-awareness is present but light, keeping it at 8 rather than higher.
